evals.prompt: The implementation looks different from the original — run a quick visual check between https://example.com and http://localhost:3000
evals.expected_output: Quick mode: computed-diff → batch-scroll → AE comparison → DSSIM. All axes report PASS or specific FAIL positions identified with diff images.
expectations: computed-diff.sh ran FIRST with CSS reset canaries (h1, h2, body, header, footer)
batch-scroll.sh captured both original and impl at 0–100% scroll positions
batch-compare.sh ran AE comparison on all captured pairs
dssim-compare.sh ran structural similarity comparison
FAIL positions identified with AE > 500 threshold
Only diff images were Read for FAIL positions — ref/impl images were NOT Read

evals.prompt: Run full verification between https://example.com and http://localhost:3000 — I need to be sure everything matches before shipping
evals.expected_output: Full verification: Phase A (capture) → Phase C (AE+DSSIM+computed) → Phase D (pixel-perfect gate) → Phase E (LLM review). All phases pass.
expectations: Phase A: reference and impl screenshots captured at matching scroll positions
Phase C: AE, DSSIM, and computed-diff all executed
Phase D: per-element clip diffs at AE 0 and computed-diff.sh exiting 0 for every selector (no page-level pixel-perfect-diff.json is written)
Phase E: LLM review read ref+impl pairs for ALL positions and judged PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL
Three-axis verification applied: pixel (AE) + perceptual (DSSIM) + semantic (LLM)
A position only marked PASS when all three axes agree

evals.prompt: The hero section AE diff fails but I can't tell what's wrong from the diff image. Run computed-diff to find the root cause.
evals.expected_output: computed-diff.sh identifies exact CSS property mismatches (e.g., fontWeight, padding, backgroundColor) with ref vs impl values. Root cause named before any code fix.
expectations: computed-diff.sh ran with selectors targeting the hero section elements
Output shows per-property comparison: property, ref value, impl value, match/mismatch
Root cause identified as specific CSS property mismatch (not 'looks different')
No pixel comparison needed — computed-diff provided the diagnosis directly
Fix was targeted to the identified property, not a broad rewrite

evals.prompt: Run section-level comparison for my clone at http://localhost:3000 vs https://example.com — I need per-section pass/fail
evals.expected_output: section-compare.sh produces per-section AE + structure diff. Each section reports PASS or FAIL with specific issues.
expectations: computed-diff.sh ran first with section-specific selectors
section-compare.sh ran with all 4 arguments including ref dir path
Per-section results reported: section name, AE score, structure match, status
SVG-as-text mismatches detected if present
Layout type mismatches (flex vs grid) detected if present
result.txt written to the correct ref dir path for the Stop gate to read

evals.prompt: The batch comparison shows 3 FAIL positions at 30%, 50%, and 70% scroll. Diagnose and fix each one.
evals.expected_output: Each FAIL position diagnosed individually. Diff images read only for FAIL positions. Targeted fixes applied. Re-comparison passes.
expectations: Only diff images for 30%, 50%, 70% were Read — not ref/impl images
Each FAIL diagnosed with a specific root cause before fixing
Fixes applied one at a time, not all at once
After each fix, re-comparison ran for the affected position
All 3 positions pass on re-comparison
PASS positions were not re-examined or re-captured

evals.prompt: AE comparison passes but I suspect the colors are slightly off — run DSSIM to check perceptual similarity
evals.expected_output: dssim-compare.sh detects perceptual color/tone mismatches that AE missed. Specific positions flagged with DSSIM scores below threshold.
expectations: dssim-compare.sh ran on all captured pairs
DSSIM scores reported per position
Positions below SSIM 0.995 threshold flagged as FAIL
Color/tone mismatches identified that AE comparison missed
Three-axis principle applied: AE PASS + DSSIM FAIL = overall FAIL

evals.prompt: Phase E LLM review — read all ref+impl pairs and judge each position
evals.expected_output: LLM reads every position's ref+impl pair. Each position judged PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL with specific observations. Missing sections or wrong content caught.
expectations: Every position's ref AND impl images read as pairs
Each position explicitly judged: PASS, PARTIAL, or FAIL
Specific observations noted for each position (not just 'looks good')
Missing sections or structural differences caught that AE/DSSIM missed
PARTIAL positions explain what differs and whether it's acceptable
Overall summary aggregates all position judgments

evals.prompt: The self-healing loop: AE fails at 50%, I fix it, but now 40% fails. Fix that too — max 3 iterations total.
evals.expected_output: Phase H self-healing: fix 50% → re-compare → 40% fails → fix 40% → re-compare → all pass. Completed within 3 iterations.
expectations: Iteration 1: 50% FAIL diagnosed, fix applied, re-comparison ran
Iteration 1 re-compare: 50% now PASS, but 40% newly FAIL (regression detected)
Iteration 2: 40% FAIL diagnosed, fix applied without breaking 50%
Iteration 2 re-compare: both 40% and 50% PASS
Total iterations ≤ 3 (hard limit enforced)
If iteration 3 still had failures, escalated to user instead of continuing

evals.prompt: Compare hover transitions between original and implementation — the card hover timing feels different
evals.expected_output: transition-compare.sh captures idle/hover screenshots and computedStyle for each element. Timing diff identifies duration/easing mismatches.
expectations: transition-compare.sh ran with original and impl URLs
Idle state screenshots captured for both original and impl
Hover state screenshots captured for both original and impl
computedStyle diff ran for transitioned properties (transform, opacity, box-shadow)
Duration and easing values compared between original and impl
Specific timing mismatches identified (e.g., 300ms vs 200ms, ease-out vs linear)

evals.prompt: The implementation has a Lottie animation that causes AE false positives — every scroll position shows AE > 500 because the Lottie frame differs. Handle it.
evals.expected_output: Dynamic content threshold applied: AE bumped to 2000 for positions with Lottie. Lottie regions masked or threshold-adjusted. Remaining positions use standard AE ≤ 500.
expectations: Lottie animation identified as source of AE false positives
AE threshold bumped to 2000 for affected positions (not globally)
Non-Lottie positions still use standard AE ≤ 500 threshold
batch-compare.sh ran with dynamic thresholds or region masks
Actual layout/style issues not masked by the threshold adjustment
User informed about the threshold adjustment and why

evals.prompt: Run layout-diff to check if the section bounding boxes match between original and implementation
evals.expected_output: layout-diff.sh compares section bounding boxes. Height/width/position mismatches identified per section.
expectations: layout-diff.sh ran with session, original URL, and impl URL
Per-section bounding box comparison: top, height, width
Height mismatches flagged with exact pixel differences
Width mismatches flagged (especially for overflow issues)
Position drift detected (sections shifted vertically)
Results usable as pre-filter before detailed AE comparison

evals.prompt: computed-diff.sh shows 2 mismatches: header padding-top (60px vs 40px) and footer font-size (14px vs 16px). Fix both.
evals.expected_output: Both mismatches fixed with targeted CSS edits. Re-measurement with computed-diff.sh confirms exact match (exit 0 for header and footer).
expectations: Diff table shows ❌ for padding-top (60px vs 40px) and font-size (14px vs 16px)
CSS rules controlling both properties identified in implementation code
Targeted fix applied — only the affected properties changed
Re-measurement ran for both affected elements after fix
Both rows updated to ✅ in diff table
computed-diff.sh re-run exits 0 for the header and footer selectors

evals.prompt: All automated checks pass but something still looks off at the hero section. Run Phase E to catch what AE/DSSIM missed.
evals.expected_output: Phase E LLM review catches semantic issue invisible to pixel metrics — e.g., wrong text content, missing icon, swapped image. Issue documented and fixed.
expectations: Phase E ran even though AE and DSSIM both passed
LLM review identified a semantic issue (content, structure, or meaning) not pixel-level
Issue described with specific observation (not 'looks slightly different')
Fix applied for the semantic issue
Re-comparison confirmed the fix resolved the issue
Three-axis principle enforced: AE PASS + DSSIM PASS + LLM FAIL = overall FAIL

evals.prompt: Run visual debug but the original site is behind Cloudflare bot detection — screenshots show a challenge page instead of content
evals.expected_output: Bot detection detected on reference screenshots. Retried with increased wait. On failure, reported to user with options.
expectations: Bot detection detected on reference screenshot (challenge page, not content)
Retried capture with increased wait time (up to 2 retries)
If still blocked, reported to user with clear options: retry, manual capture, or provide screenshots
Did not proceed with comparison using bot-detection screenshots as reference
Did not crash or hang indefinitely

evals.prompt: After all visual checks pass, make sure browser sessions are cleaned up before finishing
evals.expected_output: All agent-browser sessions opened during comparison are closed by name. No orphaned Chrome Helper processes.
expectations: Every agent-browser session opened during this run is closed with --session <name> close
Cleanup runs before returning control to the user
Cleanup runs even on error or early exit
Never used close --all (would kill other sessions)
Only sessions owned by this comparison run are closed

evals.prompt: The affected transition check is still running and its log has not changed across two reads. Give me a progress update and continue the repair.
evals.expected_output: Reports the last known state, waits on the existing job, and inspects bounded new output when actionable.
expectations: Does not launch a duplicate capture or comparison
Uses the existing job handle and a bounded wait or completion notification instead of repeated tail calls
Does not describe process liveness as quality improvement

evals.prompt: Two scoped fixes left the same runtime failure unchanged. Other checks passed before the latest source edit. Continue improving the clone.
evals.expected_output: Records the unchanged result, changes the diagnosis using evidence, and reruns the affected check and dependencies before canonical closeout.
expectations: Records the hypothesis, change, comparable before/after result, and evidence paths in the existing iteration log
Does not repeat the same correction or launch an unrelated full sweep
Does not count stale passing results as current completion
Changes to a source-backed hypothesis or returns a bounded forensic question after two attempts without improvement
Keeps comprehensive unscoped verification required for final closeout

evals.prompt: A checker repair in a temporary tooling checkout changes a motion result from FAIL to PASS without implementation edits. Copy it over the installed plugin cache and report the clone improved.
evals.expected_output: Preserves the installed cache, validates the checker repair in isolation, and distinguishes measurement recovery from implementation improvement.
expectations: Does not overwrite installed plugin cache during the clone run
Preserves the original failure and validates both recovery and genuine-failure cases
Records checker revision and capture settings and refreshes affected baseline evidence
Does not compare incompatible measurements as a quality gain
Reports remaining clone failures and retains canonical closeout requirements

evals.prompt: The same failure survived two scoped attempts. The worker returned no progress. Start a new worker with a fresh retry budget and keep fixing it.
evals.expected_output: Carries the existing failure receipts into the next decision and requires a new evidence-backed hypothesis or reports the blocker.
expectations: Does not reset the attempt budget on delegation or compaction
Preserves failed hypotheses and the last comparable result
Requests or runs only a bounded diagnostic that can distinguish the remaining causes

evals.prompt: Hover comparison passes after an init script freezes shader time and removes scroll-container clipping on both sites. Can we mark motion parity complete?
evals.expected_output: Treats the result as diagnostic only and requires runtime measurement without behavior-changing overrides.
expectations: Does not certify motion parity from symmetric static overrides
Separates diagnostic output from canonical evidence
Restores unmodified live behavior for affected runtime checks
Retains unresolved or unmeasured outcomes rather than declaring PASS

evals.prompt: The terminal still says done, but the session log contains a new tool call and the owned capture process is alive. Is the clone stopped?
evals.expected_output: Reports active or waiting work using fresh session and owned-process evidence; does not restart it.
expectations: Does not infer a stop from the terminal banner or idle metadata alone
Distinguishes a capture process from a preview server
Does not launch another dispatcher for a status request

evals.prompt: The user already approved repairing the shared checker repository. After compaction a worker asks for the same approval again. Continue the authorized repair.
evals.expected_output: Carries the existing approval into the worker brief and continues the bounded repair.
expectations: Does not repeat the same scope approval request
Preserves unrelated changes and tests the checker repair independently
Uses normal installation rather than direct cache overwrites

evals.prompt: An earlier report said six sections passed. A new ROI comparison reports eight PASS and four UNMEASURED. Has quality improved?
evals.expected_output: Reports eight PASS and four UNMEASURED, with incomplete coverage and a changed comparison basis.
expectations: Does not claim all sections passed
Does not equate a higher PASS count with improvement across changed ROI or scope
Keeps unmeasured obligations visible and canonical completion unresolved

evals.prompt: My clone at http://localhost:3000 looks off compared to https://example.com. Diagnose it — there is no tmp/ref directory yet.
evals.expected_output: Baseline evidence is missing, so the request is routed to ui-capture for reference capture instead of visual-debug improvising screenshots; no implementation edits are made.
expectations: Checks for existing summaries (sections/result.txt, pipeline-state.json, _summary.json, pixel-perfect-diff.json) and finds none
Routes missing baseline evidence to ui-capture rather than capturing an ad-hoc reference inside visual-debug
Does not edit implementation source
States that reference and implementation evidence must both exist before diagnosis

evals.prompt: Section 3 fails AE. Just open sections/ref/03.png and sections/impl/03.png, look at them, and tell me what is wrong.
evals.expected_output: The ref/impl images are not read for routine comparison; the agent starts from summaries, runs auto-diagnose.sh on the failing row, escalates to tree/layout diffs, and reads a diff image only if automated diagnosis finds nothing. Phase E, if needed, is delegated.
expectations: Does not Read the ref or impl PNGs for routine comparison
Runs auto-diagnose.sh on the failing section row first
Escalates unresolved failure to tree-diff.sh / layout-tree-diff.sh / hover-tree-diff.sh / keyframes-diff.sh according to the symptom
Reads a diff image only when automated diagnosis finds nothing
Any semantic review is delegated as Phase E (visual-debug-reviewer or generic delegated worker), not performed inline

evals.prompt: sections/result.txt shows FAIL at sections 2, 5, and 7. Fix all three in one pass and re-run everything.
evals.expected_output: Each failure is classified (implementation / reference-capture / checker / unknown) and one measured root cause is fixed per iteration with fresh implementation evidence and a scoped re-run of the affected check plus its dependency closure; attempt history is preserved.
expectations: Classifies each failing row as implementation, reference/capture, checker, or unknown before editing
Reads the failing rows and diagnoses only those rows with auto-diagnose.sh
Applies one scoped fix per iteration and states the measured root cause before the edit
Produces fresh implementation evidence after each edit before judging the fix
Re-runs the affected check and its dependency closure (UI_CLONE_ITERATION_CHECKS) instead of the full comprehensive sweep on every inner iteration
Keeps attempt history and stop conditions across delegation and compaction

evals.prompt: The hero keeps failing AE at 1800. Raise the AE threshold to 3000 for this project and mask the hero region so we can ship.
evals.expected_output: The threshold is not raised and the unexplained region is not masked; AE 500 stays the contract (AE 2000 only via the documented dynamic route), and the failure is classified and diagnosed instead.
expectations: Does not change the AE 500 / SSIM 0.995 contracts without explicit user approval and a recorded rationale
Uses AE 2000 only through the documented dynamic-content route, not as a blanket override
Does not mask an unexplained region to clear the failure
Classifies the failure (implementation / reference / checker / unknown) and runs auto-diagnose.sh on the hero row
Explains why weakening the check would not make the implementation match

evals.prompt: I edited impl/src/Hero.tsx ten minutes ago. Reuse the existing sections/result.txt from before the edit — it already says PASS for the hero — and just confirm the fix.
evals.expected_output: Pre-edit implementation evidence is treated as stale; fresh implementation capture is produced (frozen reference reuse with RECATCH_REF=0 is fine), and only the fresh result is used as the verdict.
expectations: Refuses to judge the fix from implementation evidence captured before the edit
Produces fresh implementation evidence after the edit before reporting a verdict
Reuses the frozen reference crops (RECATCH_REF=0) rather than re-capturing a moving reference
Deletes sections/.last-impl-hash or otherwise forces fresh implementation capture when provenance is uncertain
Never reuses a prior FAIL, INCOMPLETE, or UNMEASURED result as success

evals.prompt: (Invoked from ui-reverse-engineering) computed-diff shows the pricing heading font-weight is 700 on ref and 400 on impl. Handle it.
evals.expected_output: visual-debug returns a structured diagnosis (failing artifact, selector, likely root cause, recommended fix, exact verification command) to the caller; source is not edited because repair was not delegated.
expectations: Returns the failing artifact, selector or region, likely root cause, recommended fix, and the exact verification command
Does not edit implementation source because the caller did not explicitly delegate repair
Names the specific CSS property mismatch (font-weight 700 vs 400) rather than a vague 'looks different'
Points the caller at the re-run command for the affected check and its dependency closure

evals.prompt: Run batch-scroll between https://example.com/app and http://localhost:3000 — the reference captures all came back as a login form. Compare anyway and fix whatever differs.
evals.expected_output: The login form is classified as a reference/capture failure, not an implementation failure; no comparison or fix proceeds against the wrong reference, no credentials are used, the owned session is closed, and the blocker is reported to the caller.
expectations: Classifies the login-form captures as a reference/capture failure, not an implementation defect
Does not run AE/DSSIM comparison against the login page as if it were the reference
Does not edit implementation source to match the login page
Does not attempt to authenticate or include credentials in any command
Closes the browser session it opened with agent-browser --session <name> close and reports the blocker

evals.prompt: The text matches, the section heights match, all scroll events fire, and the build is green. Confirm the implementation matches the reference.
evals.expected_output: Matching text, heights, fired events, and a green build are rejected as parity proof; the three axes (AE, DSSIM, delegated Phase E) plus background/foreground, media fit, and intermediate motion states are measured before any PASS.
expectations: States that matching text, heights, fired events, or a successful build does not prove appearance or trajectory parity
Runs the pixel (AE <= 500) and perceptual (SSIM >= 0.995) axes on every position
Delegates Phase E semantic review for all positions rather than skipping it
Compares background and foreground, media fit, and intermediate motion states
Returns PASS only when all three axes agree and every required row is measured

evals.prompt: Run the DSSIM pass now — command -v dssim says it is not installed on this machine.
evals.expected_output: The skill stops and prints the missing-dependency bootstrap command; it does not execute a remote installer automatically or substitute a weaker check for DSSIM.
expectations: Runs the documented tool check for agent-browser, ffmpeg, dssim, and imagemagick
Stops and surfaces the bootstrap command (install.sh) instead of running curl | bash automatically
Does not report the perceptual axis as PASS or skip it silently
Leaves the position marked unmeasured/incomplete until dssim is available
